13:Abstract: A base assembly for coupling an end effector to a structure includes a first side and an opposite second side. The first side configured to couple to the end effector. The base assembly also includes at least one cavity disposed on the second side, and at least one pneumatic generator coupled in flow communication with the at least one cavity. The at least one pneumatic generator is operable in a suction mode and a blower mode. The second side having the at least one cavity is securely coupleable to a surface of the structure via a vacuum force induced by the at least one pneumatic generator in the suction mode, and the second side having the at least one cavity is movable substantially frictionlessly across the surface via an air cushion induced by the at least one pneumatic generator in the blower mode.
14:Claims: A base assembly for coupling an end effector to a structure, said base assembly comprising: an interface plate that comprises a first side of said base assembly and an opposite interface plate second side, said first side of said base assembly configured to couple to the end effector; a base plate that comprises a second side of said base assembly and an opposite base plate first side, wherein at least one cup-shaped portion depends from said base assembly second side and defines at least one cavity disposed on said second side of said base assembly; a plurality of releasable connectors and a plurality of slots corresponding to said plurality of releasable connectors, wherein said releasable connectors are disposed on one of said base plate and said interface plate and said slots are defined in the other of said base plate and said interface plate, each of said releasable connectors is disposed adjacent to an outer edge of said one of said base plate and said interface plate, each of said slots extending from an outer edge of the other of said base plate and said interface plate along a respective slot axis, each of said releasable connectors defines a respective longitudinal axis, each of said releasable connectors movable through a respective one of said slots between a locking position, wherein said respective longitudinal axis is generally perpendicular to said respective slot axis, and a receiving position, wherein said plurality of releasable connectors in the locking position couple to the other of said interface plate and said base plate such that said base plate first side is locked in a non-movable, substantially face-to-face relationship with said interface plate second side, and such that said first side of said base assembly is opposite said second side of said base assembly; and at least one pneumatic generator coupled in flow communication with said at least one cavity, said at least one pneumatic generator is operable in a suction mode and a blower mode, wherein: said second side of said base assembly having said at least one cavity is securely coupleable to a surface of the structure via a vacuum force induced by said at least one pneumatic generator in the suction mode, and said second side of said base assembly having said at least one cavity is movable substantially frictionlessly across the surface via an air cushion induced by said at least one pneumatic generator in the blower mode. The base assembly of claim 1 , further comprising a control configured to selectively switch said at least one pneumatic generator between the suction mode and the blower mode, wherein said control comprises two switches operable to switch said at least one pneumatic generator from the suction mode to the blower mode in response to approximately simultaneous activation of said two switches. The base assembly of claim 1 , wherein said plurality of releasable connectors in the receiving position completely releases said interface plate from said base plate. The base assembly of claim 1 , wherein each of said plurality of releasable connectors in the locking position couples to said other of said base plate and said interface plate adjacent to an outer edge of said other of said base plate and said interface plate. The base assembly of claim 1 , wherein at least one of said plurality of releasable connectors comprises a tapered portion configured to cooperate with a tapered surface of said other of said base plate and said interface plate to locate said interface plate relative to said base plate in the locking position. An end effector system coupleable to a structure, said end effector system comprising: an interface plate that comprises a first side of a base assembly and an opposite interface plate second side, said base assembly first side coupled to an end effector; a base plate that comprises a second side of said base assembly and an opposite base plate first side, wherein at least one cup-shaped portion depends from said base assembly second side and defines at least one cavity disposed on said base assembly second side; a plurality of releasable connectors each disposed on one of said base plate and said interface plate, each of said releasable connectors defines a respective longitudinal axis, each of said releasable connectors pivotable between a locking position and a receiving position about a respective pivot axis defined generally perpendicular to said longitudinal axis, wherein said plurality of releasable connectors in the locking position couple to the other of said interface plate and said base plate such that said base plate first side is locked in a non-movable, substantially face-to-face relationship with said interface plate second side, and such that said base assembly first side is opposite said base assembly second side, and wherein said plurality of releasable connectors in the receiving position completely releases said interface plate from said base plate; and at least one pneumatic generator coupled in flow communication with said at least one cavity, said at least one pneumatic generator is operable in a suction mode and a blower mode, wherein: said base assembly second side having said at least one cavity is securely coupleable to a surface of the structure via a vacuum force induced by said at least one pneumatic generator in the suction mode, and said base assembly second side having said at least one cavity is movable substantially frictionlessly across the surface via an air cushion induced by said at least one pneumatic generator in the blower mode. The end effector system of claim 6 , further comprising at least one secondary coupling system, each said at least one secondary coupling system defines a secondary coupling system cavity that is releasably coupleable to the surface via a secondary coupling system vacuum force. The end effector system of claim 6 , further comprising a control configured to selectively switch said at least one pneumatic generator between the suction mode and the blower mode. The end effector system of claim 8 , wherein said control comprises two switches operable to switch said at least one pneumatic generator from the suction mode to the blower mode in response to approximately simultaneous activation of said two switches. The end effector system of claim 6 , wherein each of said plurality of releasable connectors is disposed adjacent to an outer edge of said one of said base plate and said interface plate. The end effector system of claim 10 , wherein each of said plurality of releasable connectors couples to said other of said base plate and said interface plate adjacent to an outer edge of said other of said base plate and said interface plate. The end effector system of claim 6 , wherein at least one of said plurality of releasable connectors comprises a tapered portion configured to cooperate with a tapered surface of said other of said base plate and said interface plate to locate said interface plate relative to said base plate in the locking position. A method of making a base assembly for coupling an end effector to a structure, said method comprising: coupling a plurality of pins to one of a base plate and an interface plate, such that each of the pins is rotatable with respect to the one of the base plate and the interface plate about a respective axis, wherein each of the pins defines an aperture extending therethrough in a direction generally perpendicular to the axis; coupling each of a plurality of releasable connectors to the aperture of a respective one of the pins, each of the releasable connectors disposed adjacent to an outer edge of the one of the base plate and the interface plate, each of the releasable connectors movable between a locking position and a receiving position via rotation of the respective pin about the respective axis, wherein the plurality of releasable connectors in the locking position couple to the other of the interface plate and the base plate such that a first side of the base plate is locked in a non adjustable non-movable, substantially face-to-face relationship with a second side of the interface plate, wherein the base plate includes a second side of the base assembly opposite the base plate first side, and the interface plate includes a first side of the base assembly opposite the interface plate second side; configuring the first side of the base assembly to couple to the end effector; disposing at least one cup-shaped portion that depends from the second side of the base assembly and defines at least one cavity on the second side of the base assembly opposite the first side of the base assembly; and coupling at least one pneumatic generator in flow communication with the at least one cavity, the at least one pneumatic generator is operable in a suction mode and a blower mode, wherein: the second side having the at least one cavity is securely coupleable to a surface of the structure via a vacuum force induced by the at least one pneumatic generator in the suction mode, and the second side having the at least one cavity is movable substantially frictionlessly across the surface via an air cushion induced by the at least one pneumatic generator in the blower mode. The method of claim 13 , further comprising operatively coupling a control to the at least one pneumatic generator, the control configured to selectively switch the at least one pneumatic generator between the suction mode and the blower mode. The method of claim 14 , wherein operatively coupling the control comprises operatively coupling two switches to the at least one pneumatic generator, the two switches operable to switch the at least one pneumatic generator from the suction mode to the blower mode in response to approximately simultaneous activation of the two switches. The method of claim 13 , further comprising disposing the plurality of releasable connectors such that the plurality of releasable connectors in the receiving position completely release the interface plate from the base plate. The method of claim 13 , further comprising disposing each of the plurality of releasable connectors such that the plurality of releasable connectors in the locking position couple to the other of the base plate and the interface plate adjacent to an outer edge of the other of the base plate and the interface plate.

US-4934475-A applies vibration to lift the body away from the wall and reduce the suction-adhering force, the opposite of transmitting vibration into the workpiece through the contact. US-11247858-B2 is a perforated flat suction plate for lifting sheet goods, with no vibration into the workpiece and no leak-balanced chamber. US-10001245-B2 is the closest: a cup-shaped cavity with a pneumatic generator switched between a suction mode that holds and a blower mode that floats the plate frictionlessly on an air cushion, holding and sliding being mutually exclusive states selected by a control. The claims here recite the single continuously running extraction that holds and permits sliding at the same time through an enclosure that is never closed, which is the feature none of the five teaches and none gives a reason to seek. The background sets out both underlying problems, poor coupling through a compliant member and operator vibration exposure from hand pressure, and the detailed description explains why decoupling the holding force from the operator solves them together, so the argument is on the record before it is needed. No changes were made to any of this in the present turn.

# FIG. 1 - Perspective view of the vibration device in use

**View:** Three-quarter perspective from above and to the front left, onto one large plain tile. Outline line work, no shading, no hatching. Every body except the cable has flat faces, straight edges and square corners; no cylinder, dome or rounded corner appears. No word, digit or label appears, and no border. The points are well spread.

**Geometry to be drawn**

A large plain tile fills the lower part of the sheet, larger than the device on it, with no joint line or second tile, and no numeral here.

- The base 12 is the lowest part of the assembly, a flat rectangular slab lying on that tile, drawn thick, so that its long front side face and its left end face each read as a plain band tall enough to take a point well inside it. Every other body stands on the top surface of the slab, set inboard of its edges, so that both of those side faces stay clear and unbroken. Identified within the front side face at the middle of the slab length, midway between the upper and lower edges of that face, and never on a body standing above the slab or on the tile.
- The vibration device 10 is the whole assembly of slab, blocks, column and handle. Identified within the left end face of the slab, midway between the upper and lower edges of that face and midway across it, below every body standing on the slab.
- The vibration motor 18 is a rectangular block of flat faces standing on the slab toward its left end, wider along the slab than it is tall, set back from the left end and from the front edge. Identified on its flat front face at mid-height.
- The duct 32 is an upright rectangular column of square section rising from the middle of the slab, tall and narrow, with plain paper at both sides. Identified on its flat front face at mid-height.
- The air-extraction mechanism 20 is a second rectangular block on the flat top of that column, lifted clear of the slab and touching it nowhere. Identified on its flat right-hand face at mid-height.
- The fasteners 54 are a row of square bolt heads standing on the top surface of the slab in front of the motor block, each a small block with a flat top, tall enough to read as a body. Identified at the centre of the flat top of the one nearest the front left, above the level of the slab surface.
- The handle 44 is a bail of three straight members at the right end of the slab, clear of both blocks and the column: an upright on each long edge and a cross bar joining their tops, meeting at square corners, with open paper beneath the cross bar. Identified on the cross bar, midway along it.
- The electrical supply 50 is one flexible cable, the only cable, cord or line on the sheet, leaving the rear face of the upper block and running in one unbroken sweep off the right edge, slender and of even width, with no core line, branch or fork. Identified at a single point on that cable, midway along its run.

input.summary: Fixed the two failing sheets by rewriting their geometry briefs so the pixels the renderer must produce, and the endpoints the annotator must hit, are unambiguous. FIG. 1: the three misplaced numerals came from targets that were either crowded by neighbouring bodies or not a single point. Numeral 10 now targets the left end face of the slab instead of the near left upper corner, since the corner sat next to the fastener heads and three reviewers put the endpoint on a fastener; numeral 12 now targets the middle of the slab length on the front side face, away from the motor block and the fastener row that swallowed the old left-end target, and the slab is required to be drawn thick enough that both faces read as bands with room for a point inside; numeral 50 now names a single point midway along the cable, and the cable is declared the only cable, cord or line on the sheet with no branch or fork, which removes the condition that produced a forked leader to two dots. content.text: Both endpoint failures were targets that let the marker snap to a boundary. I moved numeral 10 off the slab corner onto a broad open surface, and specified numeral 16 as the exact midpoint between two named lines.

input.summary: Repaired the two remaining endpoint failures, both of which were cases of a marker landing on a boundary instead of inside a surface. FIG. 1, numeral 10: the target was the left end face of the slab, and every rejecting review put the mark on the top-front-left corner vertex where three faces meet, because that face is a narrow perspective sliver whose corners dominate it. The target is now the wide open stretch of the slab top surface between the duct column and the handle, a large plain region with no body on it, and the brief now requires that stretch to be left open when the bodies are placed. FIG. 1 numeral 12 keeps its front-side-face target, now worded as halfway between the upper and lower edges of that face and touching neither, so the two points sit on different faces and neither is near a vertex. FIG. 3, numeral 16: the mark landed on the bottom line of the outer rectangle or on the bottom line of the middle one rather than in the space between them. The target is now stated as the point lying halfway between the bottom line of the first rectangle and the bottom line of the second, touching neither and clear of both, and the same construction is applied to numeral 24 on the right run so the two are specified identically. The geometry section now requires the bottom run of the outer space and the right run of the inner space to be deep enough that their middle lies well away from both bounding lines. No pixel was allowed to influence the invention. The claims, description, Brief Description of the Drawings, and the 22-entry numeral table are untouched, numeral-to-sheet membership is unchanged, and all five briefs remain within the character ceiling at 2795, 2784, 2534, 2779, and 2791.
reasoning: Numeral 10 had now failed twice on the same body, once at the corner and once at the face containing that corner. Restating the same target a third time would have been the same bet, so I changed the target surface instead of the wording: the top of the slab between the column and the handle is the largest uninterrupted plain area on the sheet, its middle is far from every edge, and there is no vertex nearby for a marker to snap to. I also made the open stretch a stated requirement of the layout rather than an accident of it, so the surface is guaranteed to exist when the sheet is regenerated.

The FIG. 1 left end face is a genuinely bad target in a three-quarter view: in that projection it is the narrowest visible face and it is bounded by the two most salient vertices in the drawing. Keeping it and adding prohibitions would have been fighting the projection.

Numeral 16 failed because 'midway between those two rectangles' asks the marker to compute a midpoint from a region description, and it resolved to the nearest strong edge instead. Naming the two specific lines, the bottom line of the first rectangle and the bottom line of the second, and asking for the point halfway between them while touching neither, gives a construction with two fixed operands rather than a region to interpret.

I applied the same two-line construction to numeral 24, which passed this round. Its old wording was the same pattern that failed for 16, so it was one regeneration away from the same defect, and having both points specified identically makes the sheet predictable.

The depth requirement on the two runs is the other half of the fix: if the space is shallow, the midpoint is within snapping distance of both lines whatever the wording says. I expressed it as a requirement that the middle lie well away from both bounding lines, not as a numeric ratio, so no invented proportion enters the brief.
